item_name: Behavioral Symptom—Presence and Frequency: Physical behavioral symptoms directed toward others

lookback_source.quote: Review the medical record for the 7-day look-back period.

lookback_notes: The item's own Steps for Assessment and Coding Instructions state a 7-day look-back period ("if the behavior was exhibited 1-3 days of the last 7 days"). Per the general convention, the ARD is the last day of the observation period and the window is ARD plus the 6 previous calendar days (rai-manual-v1.20.1, p. 2-21: "ARD + 6 previous calendar days"). The section Intent also frames the items as identifying "behavioral symptoms in the last seven days" (p. E-1).

coding_levels.label: Behavior not exhibited
coding_levels.definition: If the behavioral symptoms were not present in the last 7 days. Use this code if the symptom has never been exhibited or if it previously has been exhibited but has been absent in the last 7 days.

source.quote: Code 0, behavior not exhibited: if the behavioral symptoms were not present in the last 7 days. Use this code if the symptom has never been exhibited or if it previously has been exhibited but has been absent in the last 7 days.

coding_levels.label: Behavior of this type occurred 1-3 days
coding_levels.definition: If the behavior was exhibited 1-3 days of the last 7 days, regardless of the number or severity of episodes that occur on any one of those days.

source.quote: Code 1, behavior of this type occurred 1-3 days: if the behavior was exhibited 1-3 days of the last 7 days, regardless of the number or severity of episodes that occur on any one of those days.

coding_levels.label: Behavior of this type occurred 4-6 days, but less than daily
coding_levels.definition: If the behavior was exhibited 4-6 of the last 7 days, regardless of the number or severity of episodes that occur on any of those days.

source.quote: Code 2, behavior of this type occurred 4-6 days, but less than daily: if the behavior was exhibited 4-6 of the last 7 days, regardless of the number or severity of episodes that occur on any of those days.

coding_levels.label: Behavior of this type occurred daily
coding_levels.definition: If the behavior was exhibited daily, regardless of the number or severity of episodes that occur on any of those days.

source.quote: Code 3, behavior of this type occurred daily: if the behavior was exhibited daily, regardless of the number or severity of episodes that occur on any of those days.

federal_coding_rules.rule: E0200A captures physical behavioral symptoms directed toward others (e.g., hitting, kicking, pushing, scratching, grabbing, abusing others sexually); enter the frequency code in the box.

source.quote: A. Physical behavioral symptoms directed toward others (e.g., hitting, kicking, pushing, scratching, grabbing, abusing others sexually)

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code based on whether the symptoms occurred and not based on an interpretation of the behavior's meaning, cause or the assessor's judgment that the behavior can be explained or should be tolerated.

source.quote: Code based on whether the symptoms occurred and not based on an interpretation of the behavior's meaning, cause or the assessor's judgment that the behavior can be explained or should be tolerated.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code the behavior as present even if staff have become used to the behavior or view it as typical or tolerable.

source.quote: Code as present, even if staff have become used to the behavior or view it as typical or tolerable.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Behaviors in these categories should be coded as present or not present, whether or not they might represent a rejection of care.

source.quote: Behaviors in these categories should be coded as present or not present, whether or not they might represent a rejection of care.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Resident intent must not be taken into account when coding items in Section E; the section focuses on the resident's actions, not the intent of the behavior.

source.quote: Resident intent should not be taken into account when coding for items in this section.

federal_coding_rules.rule: The frequency code reflects the number of days the behavior occurred within the 7-day look-back period, not the number or severity of episodes on any given day.

source.quote: Coding: E0200A would be coded 1, behavior of this type occurred 1-3 days of the last 7 days.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Coding of E0200A determines downstream items: if E0200A, E0200B, and E0200C are all coded 0, code E0300 as 0 (no) and skip to E0800; if any of E0200A, E0200B, or E0200C were coded 1, 2, or 3, code E0300 as 1 (yes) and complete E0500 and E0600.

source.quote: Code 0, no: if E0200A, E0200B, and E0200C all are coded 0, not present. Skip to Rejection of Care—Presence & Frequency item (E0800).

federal.criterion: Medical record reviewed for the 7-day look-back period to identify presence and frequency of physical behavioral symptoms directed toward others.

source.quote: Review the medical record for the 7-day look-back period.

federal.notes: Listed as step 1 of Steps for Assessment for E0200.

federal.criterion: Staff across all shifts and disciplines, as well as others with close interactions with the resident during the 7-day look-back period (including family or friends who visit frequently), were interviewed.

source.quote: Interview staff, across all shifts and disciplines, as well as others who had close interactions with the resident during the 7-day look-back period, including family or friends who visit frequently or have frequent contact with the resident.

federal.notes: Step 2 of Steps for Assessment for E0200.

federal.criterion: Resident observed in a variety of situations during the 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Observe the resident in a variety of situations during the 7-day look-back period.

federal.notes: Step 3 of Steps for Assessment for E0200.

federal.criterion: Documentation supports comparison of subsequent assessments to baseline to identify changes in the resident's behavior, including response to interventions.

source.quote: Subsequent assessments and documentation can be compared to baseline to identify changes in the resident's behavior, including response to interventions.

federal.notes: Stated under Planning for Care rationale rather than as a required documentation element.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied pages for E0200 do not tie this item to any payment or case-mix classification.
